Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 ↗

Regulation 5(14) provides for a separate “Contains” declaration for specified foods and ingredients known to cause allergy, and states that presence of allergenic ingredients due to cross-contamination may be declared separately as “May Contains”.

Food Safety and Standards Authority of India · India; original Gazette notification for packaged-food labelling · Published 2020-11-17 · Retrieved 21/10/2026

This is the original Gazette notification, not a current consolidated legal determination. Later amendments, directions, product-specific exceptions and effective dates must be checked live before judging current applicability or compliance. The label wording does not establish a particular package’s contents, allergen amount or exposure, individual risk or safety.

NUTRISCAN SUMMARY · CHECK ORIGINAL SOURCE
FAQ on Food Safety and Standards (Labelling & Display) Regulations, 2020 ↗

FSSAI distinguishes allergenic ingredients declared separately as “Contains [allergen]” from allergen presence due to cross-contamination, which may be declared separately as “May Contains [allergen]”. Its FAQ says the illustrated wording is not exclusive and that wording with a similar meaning may be used, including “May contain traces of [allergen]” or a statement that the product is made in a facility that processes that allergen.

Food Safety and Standards Authority of India · India; FSSAI interpretation of packaged-food labelling · Published 2023-11-01 · Retrieved 21/10/2026

This dated FAQ explains label wording; it does not establish that a particular allergen is actually present, its amount or exposure, individual risk or safety, or whether a package complies. Check the current regulation, subsequent amendments or directions, exact product type and circumstances through live official research before making a legal determination.
outcomes.whoSourceText:
Evidence · Carbohydrate intake for adults and children: WHO guideline
NUTRISCAN SUMMARY · CHECK ORIGINAL SOURCE
Carbohydrate intake for adults and children: WHO guideline ↗

WHO recommends adults consume at least 25 g/day of naturally occurring dietary fibre and 400 g/day of vegetables and fruits; for children and adolescents it suggests at least 15 g/day at ages 2–5, 21 g/day at ages 6–9, and 25 g/day at ages 10 or older. It recommends that carbohydrate come primarily from whole grains, vegetables, fruits and pulses.

World Health Organization · Global; population dietary guidance · Published 2023-07-17 · Retrieved 21/10/2026

Population guidance for whole-diet quality, not a package-specific threshold, individualized prescription, or treatment target. Naturally occurring fibre guidance refers to fibre as consumed in foods and cannot be directly equated with a packaged-food fibre declaration; a single product cannot establish daily diet adequacy.
